claim: Cancer treatment failure often results from tumor evolution, both genotypic and phenotypic, away from sensitive cell states.
source: This failure often results from tumor evolution, both genotypic and phenotypic, away from sensitive cell states.
evidence: This is stated as a general assertion in the abstract about cancer treatment failure mechanisms.

claim: The optimal cancer evasion strategy results in increased cancer evasion rates compared to a passive, fixed strategy.
source: We solve for the unique optimal cancer evasion strategy using stochastic dynamic programming and demonstrate that this policy results in increased cancer evasion rates compared to a passive, fixed strategy.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by mathematical modeling and simulations.

claim: Optimally adaptive evaders navigating varying selective environments result in substantially heterogeneous post-escape tumor antigenicity, giving rise to immunogenically hot and cold tumors.
source: In contrast with a passive strategy, optimally adaptive evaders navigating varying selective environments result in substantially heterogeneous post-escape tumor antigenicity, giving rise to immunogenically hot and cold tumors.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by model predictions shown in figures.

claim: Prior research has made substantial progress in detailing the mathematics of acquired drug resistance.
source: Prior research efforts have made substantial progress in detailing the mathematics of acquired drug resistance (Iwasa et al., 2006; Michor et al., 2004; Komarova, 2006) and the complementary roles of phenotypic and genotypic changes (Gupta et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Immunotherapy breakthroughs have generated considerable interest in quantifying the cancer-immune interaction.
source: These latter breakthroughs have generated considerable interest in quantifying the cancer-immune interaction (Mayer et al., 2019; Sontag, 2017; George et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Tumors can evade the immune system via either elimination or downregulation of tumor-associated antigens normally detectable by the T cell repertoire.
source: As with targeted therapeutic resistance via compensatory evolution or adaptive rewiring (Bergholz and Zhao, 2021), tumors can similarly evade the immune system via either elimination or downregulation of tumor-associated antigens (TAAs) normally detectable by the T cell repertoire (Rosenthal et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Dynamical changes in cancer genotypes and phenotypes create additional TAAs that may subsequently be recognized by distinct T cells.
source: Dynamical changes in cancer genotypes and phenotypes, while problematic for conventional therapies, create additional TAAs that may subsequently be recognized by distinct T cells (Yarchoan et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The evolving diversity of the T cell repertoire provides adaptive immunity and immunotherapy the unique advantage of repeated tumor recognition opportunities.
source: Thus, the evolving diversity of the T cell repertoire, consisting of billions of unique clones each with a distinct T cell receptor, provides adaptive immunity and immunotherapy the unique advantage of repeated tumor recognition opportunities (George and Levine, 2021; Lakatos et al., 2020; Qi et al., 2014), making long-term evasion more challenging.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work and represents established knowledge about T cell diversity.

claim: There is increasing evidence of significant and sustained tumor evolution driven by immune surveillance.
source: These works were based on increasing evidence of significant and sustained tumor evolution driven by immune surveillance (Turajlic et al., 2018; Jamal-Hanjani et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Immunosurveillance via distinct T cell clones imposes an adaptive, stochastic recognition environment on developing cancer populations.
source: Immunosurveillance via distinct T cell clones imposes an adaptive, stochastic recognition environment on developing cancer populations (Desponds et al., 2016) that can result either in cancer elimination, escape, or equilibrium (Schreiber et al., 2002; Dunn et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Equilibrium results in cancer co-existence with the immune system over large time scales.
source: Equilibrium results in cancer co-existence with the immune system over large time scales (Turajlic et al., 2018), thereby motivating the need for a more complete understanding of the interplay between immune recognition and cancer evolution for effective therapeutic design.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Previous modeling efforts have assumed that cancer adaptation occurs passively, without behavior predicated on knowledge of the current immune microenvironment.
source: Previous modeling efforts have assumed that cancer adaptation occurs passively, that is, without behavior predicated on knowledge of the current immune microenvironment (IME).
evidence: This is a statement about prior modeling approaches.

claim: Cancer populations commonly undergo phenotypic changes capable of altering their immunogenicity.
source: However, it is well known that cancer populations commonly undergo phenotypic changes capable of altering their immunogenicity (Tripathi et al., 2016); these changes could be coupled to sensing of the IME in a manner similar to cancer mechanical, chemical, and stress sensing (Lee et al., 2019; Damaghi et al., 2013; Rosenberg, 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Direct experimental evidence demonstrates genetic adaptation in bacterial systems capable of sensing stress and consequently varying the per-cell mutation rate.
source: Moreover, direct experimental evidence demonstrates genetic adaptation in bacterial systems capable of sensing stress and consequently varying the per-cell mutation rate (Al Mamun et al., 2012; Rosenberg and Queitsch, 2014); there appear to be similar stress pathways in cancer (Bindra et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: The TEAL model describes a discrete-time stochastic process tracking the number of targets available to a recognizing adaptive immune system.
source: The TEAL model describes a discrete-time stochastic process tracking the number of targets available to a recognizing adaptive immune system.
evidence: This is a description of the model developed in this work.

claim: The optimal evasion strategy that maximizes long-run population survival is the unique solution.
source: In doing so, we obtain an exact analytical characterization of the evasion policy that maximizes long-run population survival, which we show is the unique solution.
evidence: This is a mathematical result proven in the manuscript.

claim: Optimized strategies exhibit substantial diversity in their dynamical behavior, distinguishing them from threats with a fixed evolutionary strategy.
source: Surprisingly, we find that optimized strategies exhibit substantial diversity in their dynamical behavior, distinguishing them from threats with a fixed evolutionary strategy.
evidence: This is a finding from the model analysis.

claim: Immune recognition efficiency and the IME microenvironment are predicted to influence the likelihood for tumors to either accumulate or lose therapeutically actionable TAAs prior to their escape.
source: Notably, immune recognition efficiency and the IME microenvironment are predicted to influence the likelihood for tumors to either accumulate or lose therapeutically actionable TAAs prior to their escape.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model.

claim: Strong immune selective pressure in early cancer development results in tumor neoantigen depletion and is prognostic of poor clinical outcome.
source: This prediction agrees with recent empirical observations that strong immune selective pressure in early cancer development results in tumor neoantigen depletion and is prognostic of poor clinical outcome (Rosenthal et al., 2019; Lakatos et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior empirical work.

claim: If the immune system cannot detect any of the available TAAs in a given period, then the cancer population escapes detection.
source: If the immune system cannot detect any of the available TAAs in a given period, then the cancer population escapes detection.
evidence: This is a model definition.

claim: If evasion balances recognition and all detected antigens are lost, then equilibrium (non-escape, non-elimination) ensues.
source: If evasion balances recognition and all detected antigens are lost, then equilibrium (non-escape, non-elimination) ensues, and the process repeats in the next period with a new number of target antigens given by a state transition equation
evidence: This is a model definition.

claim: The model framework mirrors the outcomes resulting from known tumor-immune interactions, a process that leads via immunoediting to cancer escape, elimination, or equilibrium.
source: This framework mirrors the outcomes resulting from known tumor-immune interactions, a process that leads via immunoediting to cancer escape, elimination, or equilibrium (Schreiber et al., 2002; Dunn et al., 2002; Dunn et al., 2004; Koebel et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim connects the model to established biological concepts and is supported by citations.

claim: Active evasion strategies enhance population survival rates compared to passive strategies.
source: Despite identical mean TAA evolution (Figure 2A) and comparable intertemporal penalties, the optimized strategy results in substantially higher cancer escape probability (150%) compared to the passive case.
evidence: This is a finding from simulations shown in Figure 2.

claim: Optimized strategies generate wider escape time distributions compared to passive strategies.
source: Moreover, optimized strategies generate wider escape time distributions, thus illustrating an adaptive evader's sustained effort to thwart elimination prior to escape (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from simulations shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Optimized immune evaders are more successful in evading detection than their passive counterparts across various recognition landscapes.
source: We simulate TEAL dynamics and find that optimized immune evaders are more successful in evading detection than their passive counterparts across various recognition landscapes (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from simulations shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Evasion in the optimized case occurs largely after a sustained interaction with the recognizing threat.
source: Evasion, when it occurs in the optimized case, does so largely after a sustained interaction with the recognizing threat (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from simulations shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The prediction of constant mutation accumulation is consistent with empirically observed cancer mutation behavior.
source: The prediction of constant accumulation is consistent with empirically observed cancer mutation behavior (Lawrence et al., 2013; Alexandrov et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim connects model predictions to empirical observations and is supported by citations.

claim: Larger penalties result in higher post-escape TAA levels.
source: Our results demonstrate that larger penalties result in higher post-escape TAA levels, while efficient immune recognition depletes available TAAs.
evidence: This is a finding from simulations shown in Figure 4.

claim: Efficient immune recognition depletes available TAAs.
source: Our results demonstrate that larger penalties result in higher post-escape TAA levels, while efficient immune recognition depletes available TAAs.
evidence: This is a finding from simulations shown in Figure 4.

claim: Escape in the presence of strong immune recognition biases the tumor to have low numbers of TAAs.
source: The presumptive reason for this latter observation is that escape in the presence of strong immune recognition biases the tumor to have low numbers of TAAs.
evidence: This is an inference from the model results.

claim: IL-6 secreted by CTLs, macrophages, and dendritic cells in response to immune recognition has been shown to directly activate ATM, a factor implicated in response to DNA damage, and this has been associated with increased metastasis and multi-drug resistance in lung cancer.
source: At the signaling level, IL-6 secreted by CTLs, macrophages, and dendritic cells in response to immune recognition has been shown to directly activate ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM), a factor implicated in response to DNA damage, and this has been associated with increased metastasis and multi-drug resistance in lung cancer (Jiang et al., 2015; Yan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: IFN-gamma released by activated CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes activates the cell-intrinsic STING pathway in response to DNA damage in cancer.
source: IFN-gamma released by activated CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes activates the cell-intrinsic STING pathway in response to DNA damage in cancer, implicating an altered TME from activated CD8+ T cells that is measurable by the cancer (Xiong et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Granzyme B release has been directly linked to DNA damage and associated CHK2 and p53 stress responses.
source: Lastly, at the level of individual TCR interactions with recognized tumor cells, granzyme B release has been directly linked to DNA damage and associated CHK2 and p53 stress responses, and studies have demonstrated hSMG-1 stress-activated proteins upregulated in cancer cells following granzyme B treatment (Meslin et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Granzyme release in the microenvironment serves a signaling molecule promoting a pro-inflammatory response from other immune cells.
source: Moreover, granzyme release in the microenvironment serves a signaling molecule promoting a pro-inflammatory response from other immune cells (Cullen et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The lower observed TAA availability of hematological malignancies vs. immune-protected solid tumors occurs as a result of greater immune accessibility and possible immunoediting of liquid cancers.
source: First, our results would suggest that the lower observed TAA availability of hematological malignancies vs. immune-protected solid tumors, such as melanoma (Lawrence et al., 2013), occurs as a result of greater immune accessibility and possible immunoediting of liquid cancers.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model that is consistent with empirical observations cited.

claim: The model predicts enhanced immune interactions resulting from increasing the cost of immune evasion in the evading cancer population in order to enrich the TAAs following escape.
source: Second, our model predicts enhanced immune interactions, both natural and treatment-derived, resulting from increasing the cost of immune evasion in the evading cancer population in order to enrich the TAAs following escape.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model.

claim: The model supports the utility of neo-adjuvant radiation therapy or chemotherapy in inducing immunogenicity.
source: This supports the utility of neo-adjuvant radiation therapy (McGranahan et al., 2016) or chemotherapy (Mouw et al., 2017) in inducing immunogenicity.
evidence: This is an inference from the model that is consistent with prior work cited.

claim: Tumor antigen depletion is a concerning consequence of immunotherapy since increased recognition is desirable and required for tumor elimination.
source: Tumor antigen depletion is a concerning consequence of immunotherapy since increased recognition is desirable and required for tumor elimination.
evidence: This is a statement about the clinical implications of the model findings.

claim: One contributor to tumor antigen depletion in solid tumors is T cell exclusion.
source: In solid tumors, one contributor to this problem is T cell exclusion (Pai et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: If effective treatment and robust tumor recognition lead to relapse, the resulting tumor has a greater chance of being TAA-depleted.
source: However, should effective treatment and robust tumor recognition lead to relapse, the resulting tumor has a greater chance of being TAA-depleted (Rosenthal et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work and is consistent with model predictions.

claim: The detrimental effect of targeting can be offset by increasing the 'hostility of the IME.'
source: Our results suggest that this detrimental effect of targeting can be offset by increasing the 'hostility of the IME.'
evidence: This is a prediction from the model.

claim: The TEAL model does not distinguish between different types of TAA loss, which may occur through a number of mechanisms, including somatic mutation, epigenetic regulation, or phenotypic alteration.
source: We do not distinguish between different types of TAA loss, which may occur through a number of mechanisms, including somatic mutation, epigenetic regulation, or phenotypic alteration.
evidence: This is a statement about the scope and limitations of the model.

claim: The TEAL model implicitly equates antigen loss and the progression of a subpopulation currently adapted to evade immune targeting as equivalent.
source: Our model implicitly equates antigen loss and the progression of a subpopulation currently adapted to evade immune targeting – either by direct pruning of the fittest subclone or by stochastic emergence and subsequent growth of a new one lacking the targeted antigens – as equivalent.
evidence: This is a statement about a model assumption.

claim: The TEAL model tracks the fittest clone represented by a core set clonal antigens.
source: Here, we tracked the fittest clone represented by a core set clonal antigens.
evidence: This is a statement about what the model tracks.

claim: Heterogeneous populations each having a distinct subclonal signature can be tracked, but the corresponding antigen-driven selection and fitness cost to each clone would be coupled through shared antigens.
source: We remark that heterogeneous populations each having a distinct subclonal signature can also be tracked, but the corresponding antigen-driven selection and fitness cost to each clone would be coupled through shared antigens (see 'Methods').
evidence: This is a statement about model extensions discussed in the methods.

claim: The intertemporal period considered represents the time period between the earliest moment that the adaptive immune system may identify a cancer clone and the latest point after which such a recognition event would no longer be able to prevent cancer escape.
source: In this discrete-time evolutionary model, the intertemporal period considered represents the time period between the earliest moment that the adaptive immune system may identify a cancer clone and the latest point after which such a recognition event would no longer be able to prevent cancer escape (George and Levine, 2020).
evidence: This is a definition of the time scale in the model, supported by a citation.

claim: Variations in individual TAA antigenicity could affect overall immunogenicity, but the model does not take this into account.
source: In addition to quantity, variations in individual TAA antigenicity could affect overall immunogenicity, but we do not as yet take this into account.
evidence: This is a statement about a model limitation.

claim: The TEAL model represents a framework broadly applicable for studying population behavior consistent with optimized collective decision-making.
source: The TEAL model represents a framework broadly applicable for studying population behavior consistent with optimized collective decision-making, and subsequent experimental validation or refutation is of highest priority.
evidence: This is a statement about the broader applicability of the model framework.

claim: The possibility that cancer population-level strategies are somewhat informed to the present recognition threat would have a radical effect on optimal treatment approach.
source: The possibility that cancer population-level strategies are somewhat informed to the present recognition threat would have a radical effect on our own optimal treatment approach.
evidence: This is a statement about the implications of the optimal escape hypothesis.
